paragraphs: Here's what Job 21 teaches, friend: honest questions are allowed in front of God. Job doesn't pretend life adds up neatly. He asks, "Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?" (Job 21:7), and he says it out loud, shaking and all. Nobody in this passage gets struck for asking.

The friends keep saying that the wicked always crash and the good always cruise. Job says look around, because that's not how every story ends (Job 21:23-26). Now, I'm not saying wickedness pays. Job himself says the prosperity of the wicked "is not in their own hands," so he stays far from their counsel (Job 21:16). The lesson is that a tidy formula can't explain every life, and a formula used on a hurting person turns into "empty words" (Job 21:34).

So when you're hurting, baker, don't let anybody hand you a neat little answer that doesn't fit. And when somebody else is hurting, listen first, because Job begged his friends to do that very thing (Job 21:2). Bring your hardest questions to God, and be patient with the answers you don't have yet. Job's story isn't finished, and neither is the teaching.
